fields.System.Title: FDN-8 — Event outbox
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Announce facts to other modules and external systems in a way that cannot lose an event or
announce something that did not happen.

Scope

In. Transactional event write, a delivery worker, retry with backoff, dead-letter handling,
pruning.

Out. A message broker. The outbox table does this job with one fewer moving part — see
[doc 10 §8](../../../docs/10-local-deployment.md).

Design notes

Why an outbox and not a direct call. If inventory calls the ERP inside the stock
transaction, a slow ERP makes receiving slow and an ERP outage makes receiving fail. Worse, if
the HTTP call succeeds and the transaction then rolls back, the ERP believes something that
never happened.

Writing the event into a table in the same transaction removes both failure modes.

You get at-least-once delivery, never exactly-once. The worker can crash after delivering
and before marking sent. Every consumer must therefore deduplicate on event_id. Document this
to whoever builds the consumer — it is easy for them to assume otherwise.

Every event carries event_id, event_type, occurred_at, aggregate_id, version,
payload, correlation_id.

Prune, or the delivery query slows every day. Index on (status, created_at) and delete
delivered rows after a retention window.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Event published before commit | [doc 09 §2.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Event lost after commit | [doc 08 §10](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Duplicate delivery breaking a non-idempotent consumer | [doc 09 §3.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Outbox never pruned | [doc 04 §3.1](../../../docs/04-modules.md) |
